# Lakhdatar Green Energy — Complete Technical & Organizational Documentation

## 1. Executive Summary
Lakhdatar Green Energy is an Indian industrial biomass pellet manufacturing enterprise established in 2010. The company operates high-capacity pelletizing infrastructure in the Industrial Area of Tilda, Raipur District, Chhattisgarh (21.5270° N, 81.7787° E). Lakhdatar specializes in manufacturing dense, high-Gross Calorific Value (GCV) biomass pellets derived from 100% sustainably aggregated agricultural residues (primarily mustard straw/husk, saw dust, and paddy straw). 

The pellets serve as a direct, carbon-neutral drop-in fuel for industrial steam boilers, thermic fluid heaters, and pulverized coal-fired thermal power plants looking to satisfy government co-firing mandates (MoP SAMARTH initiative and CAQM Delhi-NCR regulations).

## 3. Product Specifications & Fuel Comparison
### 3.1 Lakhdatar High-GCV Biomass Pellets Technical Data
- **Gross Calorific Value (GCV)**: 3,800 kcal/kg to 4,200+ kcal/kg (Gross as Received / Air Dried Basis)
- **Total Moisture**: <= 8% to 10% (by mass)
- **Ash Content**: <= 6% to 10% (dry basis)
- **Volatile Matter**: 65% to 75%
- **Fixed Carbon**: 16% to 22%
- **Bulk Density**: >= 650 kg/m³ to 720 kg/m³
- **Pellet Diameter**: 6 mm to 8 mm (+/- 1mm)
- **Pellet Length**: 10 mm to 35 mm
- **Fines Content**: <= 1.5% at dispatch
- **Sulphur (S)**: < 0.1% (virtually zero SOx emissions)
- **Chlorine (Cl)**: < 0.05% (prevents high-temperature superheater tube corrosion)

### 3.2 Biomass Pellets vs. Industrial Coal
| Parameter | High-GCV Biomass Pellets | Indian Grade E/F Coal | Imported Steam Coal |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **GCV (kcal/kg)** | 3,800 – 4,200 | 3,100 – 3,600 | 4,200 – 5,000 |
| **Ash Content** | 6 – 10% | 35 – 45% | 8 – 15% |
| **Moisture Content**| < 10% | 12 – 18% | 10 – 16% |
| **Sulphur Content** | < 0.1% | 0.5 – 1.2% | 0.6 – 1.0% |
| **Net Carbon Status**| 100% Carbon Neutral (Scope 1 Reduction) | High Net Carbon Emitter | High Net Carbon Emitter |
| **Boiler Ash Handling**| Reduced by ~75% vs Coal | Heavy Clinkering/Slagging | Moderate Ash |

## 4. Production Process (From Field to Furnace)
1. **Agri-Residue Aggregation**: Sourced directly from local farmers in Chhattisgarh and Central India, providing farmers with supplemental revenue and stopping open-field crop residue burning.
2. **Drying & Moisture Normalization**: Raw biomass is dried through rotary industrial dryers down to an optimal moisture level below 10%.
3. **Milling & Size Reduction**: Hammer mills pulverize the raw fiber to uniform 2–3mm particle size.
4. **High-Pressure Extrusion & Densification**: Ring-die pellet mills compress the biomass under extreme pressure and natural lignin thermal activation (without synthetic binders) to achieve >650 kg/m³ bulk density.
5. **Cooling & Dedusting**: Counterflow coolers stabilize the pellets; screening trommels remove fines.
6. **Laboratory Testing & Quality Verification**: Every production batch is certified for GCV, moisture, and ash content in our dedicated quality lab prior to dispatch.

## 5. Regulatory Compliance & Environmental Mandates
- **Ministry of Power (MoP) SAMARTH Mission**: Mandates 5% to 7% biomass co-firing in all coal-based thermal power plants across India.
- **Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM)**: Bans unapproved fossil fuels (petcoke, furnace oil, non-compliant coal) in Delhi-NCR and promotes 100% bio-fuel transition in industrial heating applications.
- **Scope 1 Emission Reductions**: Biomass combustion carbon is part of the short-term biogenic carbon cycle (photosynthesis absorption cycle), resulting in net zero Scope 1 emissions under GHG Protocol.
